subject: Regional SI adapter charter — EU/APAC data fence and partner responsibilities
messages:
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwoodinference.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: partners@redwoodinference.com
Date: Tue, 6 Oct 2026 09:12:00 +0000
Subject: Regional SI adapter charter — EU/APAC data fence and partner responsibilities

Team,

Summary: I sketched an "adapter" model that lets regional SIs (EU on-prem enclaves or APAC consultancies with a local enclave) implement lightweight integrations without our needing to host customer PII in non-compliant regions. The draft (attached) outlines responsibilities, minimal certs, and an SLA fallback model.

Why this matters: several prospects in EU and APAC are pushing for a partner-hosted adapter rather than Redwood-managed private deployments. If we standardize the adapter contract and data-fence expectations, we can accelerate SI onboarding and preserve our routing/caching guarantees.

Key asks for this week:
- Vanessa: review the operational responsibilities (deployment + incident escalation) in section 2 and mark anything that needs Redwood ops support.
- Naomi: legal — can you flag non-starters in the compliance checklist? Particularly around audit logs and KMS key custody.
- Soojin: partnerships — can you map the potential partner tiers (integration+certified vs partner-provisioned) and recommend pilot candidates?

Attachments: adapter-charter-draft.pdf, regional-data-flow-v2.png

I propose we run a 4-week pilot with 1 EU SI (NorthStar Systems) and 1 APAC consultancy (ZH Consult). If we get green-light, we should have a templated adapter contract and an Ops runbook ready before the pilot starts.

Thanks — Tessa

--
Tessa Morgan
Head of Partnerships, Redwood Inference
tessa.morgan@redwoodinference.com | +1 (415) 555-0183

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwoodinference.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 6 Oct 2026 11:03:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Regional SI adapter charter — EU/APAC data fence and partner responsibilities

Thanks Tessa — quick read and a few notes inline (see attachment comments). High level: I like the adapter-rights model (we keep control of model routing + tokens; partner hosts ephemeral session handling). A couple of operational points:

- Incident ownership: we should require a 2-hour acknowledgment SLA from the SI and a 4-hour mitigation window for P0 customer-facing incidents. Anything longer and Redwood must have right-to-intervene.
- Monitoring: partners must push a minimal set of telemetry (latency + error rates + anonymized token counts) into our ingest endpoint. We can't accept raw logs that contain user-provided text.
- Escrow: in the EU pilot, we should include an escrow pathway for keys if the partner is unable to meet uptime SLA for 7 consecutive days. Naomi — can the legal team draft a limited escrow clause?

I also flagged a required change to the data-flow diagram: where partner buffers ephemeral inputs, mark a TTL of 120s and explicit deletion events.

I'll join the pilot candidate call and can support runbook steps for incident response.

Vanessa

--
Vanessa Ortiz
Senior Strategic Partnerships Manager, Redwood Inference
vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com

From: Trevor Mills <trevor.mills@northstarsys.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwoodinference.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Mei Chen <mei.chen@zhconsult.co.jp>
Date: Tue, 6 Oct 2026 14:27:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Regional SI adapter charter — EU/APAC data fence and partner responsibilities

Tessa / Vanessa — thanks for sharing, and appreciate the clarity. NorthStar is open to a pilot. Quick responses to the draft:

- SLA: the 2-hour ack / 4-hour mitigation is tight for our standard managed services in some EU countries due to on-call rotations; we can commit to a 4-hour ack / 8-hour mitigation for the pilot, with escalation to a Redwood-run fallback after 12 hours. Is that acceptable for a timeboxed pilot?
- Certification: we can complete a SOC-lite audit and provide a signed attestation for least-privilege KMS usage. We would ask Redwood for a short list of must-have audit items (logs retention, access control evidence).
- Connectivity: for APAC (Mei cc'd), we need a lightweight connectivity test harness. Mei — can your team stand up a stub that validates TLS mutual auth and a token-based handshake?

We're happy to run the first integration with a single vertical customer (finance SaaS) that requested local processing. If legal needs a redline of the adapter contract, send a tracked copy and we'll have our counsel review.

Best,
Trevor

--
Trevor Mills
Director, Cloud Integrations | NorthStar Systems
trevor.mills@northstarsys.com | +44 20 7946 0182

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwoodinference.com>
To: Trevor Mills <trevor.mills@northstarsys.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 6 Oct 2026 16:45:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Regional SI adapter charter — EU/APAC data fence and partner responsibilities

Trevor — great, thanks. Short responses and next steps below.

- SLA: acceptable for a 6-week timeboxed pilot: NorthStar commits to 4-hour ack / 8-hour mitigation; Redwood will provide a defined fallback path that can be triggered after 12 hours. We'll capture this as a pilot exception and re-evaluate for standard certification.
- Legal checklist: Naomi — please add an "SOC-lite" bucket and an escrow-trigger section (trigger = 7-day SLA breach) to the draft. We need a one-pager that both partners can sign for the pilot.
- Connectivity harness: Mei (cc'd) — can you schedule a 60-minute connectivity dry-run the week of Oct 12? If so, we'll circulate the test plan (mutual TLS + token handshake + sample TTL deletion).

Proposed timeline:
1) Oct 8 — internal alignment meeting (30m) to finalize runbook and owner list. Link: Calendar: 2026-10-08T15:00:00Z-regional-integration-sync
2) Oct 12–14 — connectivity dry-run with NorthStar and ZH Consult
3) Oct 19 — pilot go/no-go decision

Owners:
- Ops runbook: Vanessa
- Legal & escrow clause: Naomi
- Partner engagement & scheduling: Soojin
- Engineering contact (integration hooks): Vivek Kulkarni (I will loop him into the next thread)

Thanks everyone — I will attach the updated charter after Naomi and Vanessa's inputs and set the Oct 8 15:00 sync.

Cheers,
Tessa

--
Tessa Morgan
Head of Partnerships, Redwood Inference
tessa.morgan@redwoodinference.com | +1 (415) 555-0183
